- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or high-value periods.
- Underestimates during prolonged downward trends or when true values dip below 35–40.
- Overreacts to recent high values, overshooting by 2–5 points in the immediate next period.
- Fails to capture mean reversion in the 30-day window — tends to hold high values longer than observed.
- Shows lag in adjusting to true price drops, often missing the first 3–5 days of a downward trend.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum, especially when true values show volatility or sudden reversals.
- Underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks in the 10–15 day horizon.
- Tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp drops or spikes in the final 5–10 days of the forecast.
